headline.title: This week at a glance
headline.summary: The Ebola Bundibugyo outbreak continues to accelerate in DRC and Uganda. As of 24 May, cases exceed 650 suspected with 160+ deaths confirmed and probable. CDC's Title 42 entry restrictions now in effect. The MV Hondius cruise-ship hantavirus cluster remains under international contact-tracing. Mpox clade Ib sustains endemic transmission across EU/EEA with documented vaccination gaps.
headline.takeaway: The Bundibugyo ebolavirus remains the dominant global public health emergency. As of May 24, DRC and Uganda have reported 650+ suspected cases with 160+ confirmed and probable deaths. The outbreak shows no sign of slowing: 26 new confirmed cases and 143 new suspected cases were identified in the 24–48 hours preceding the 19 May briefing, and a US physician working in Bunia was medevaced to Germany after testing positive. The first American case has galvanized US entry restrictions — CDC invoked Title 42 for the first time since COVID-19 on 18 May, suspending non-US national entry from DRC, Uganda and South Sudan for 30 days. No approved Bundibugyo-specific therapeutics or vaccines exist; Africa CDC and WHO are convening urgent expert review for emergency-use trials of investigational monoclonal antibodies, remdesivir, and pre-clinical vaccine candidates. The MV Hondius Andes hantavirus cluster (10 confirmed/probable, 3 deaths) reached Rotterdam on 18 May; the contact-tracing window spans 19 countries across six weeks. No symptomatic disembarkees were identified on arrival. Mpox clade Ib continues endemic circulation in Europe — 80 clade I cases in 10 EU/EEA countries in March, with only 23% of reported cases fully vaccinated. This week's focus: urgently establish emergency investigational countermeasures (ICM) protocols for Bundibugyo; coordinate international contact-tracing and clinical-alert pathways for hantavirus; sustain targeted vaccination for at-risk MSM populations for mpox.

pathogens.name: Ebola Bundibugyo
pathogens.scientific_name: Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BVD) — DRC Ituri outbreak with cross-border spread to Uganda and first American case
pathogens.location: DRC Ituri Province (Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu) · Kampala, Uganda · medevac of US doctor to Germany

stats.label: Suspected cases (DRC + Uganda as of 24 May)

pathogens.why: The PHEIC declared on 16 May has escalated sharply. In nine days (15–24 May), suspected cases surged from ~246 to 650+, deaths nearly doubled from 80 to 160+, and confirmed cases more than doubled (34 → 64). The US Title 42 entry suspension on 18 May marks the first deployment of this authority since COVID-19 and signals maximal alarm. Dr. Peter Stafford, a US physician working in Bunia since 2023, was confirmed positive on 18 May and medevaced to Germany with six high-risk-contact Americans. The same day the CDC confirmed an independent second American case in Uganda. Critical gaps remain: no approved Bundibugyo-specific therapeutics or vaccines, weak contact-tracing in insecurity-affected zones, and four healthcare worker deaths in 72 hours at Mongbwalu General Referral Hospital signal catastrophic IPC failures. WHO and Africa CDC are convening R&D Blueprint expert review of candidate monoclonal antibodies, remdesivir, and BVD vaccine candidates for emergency-use clinical trials.
policy_bullets: Activate cross-border surveillance and exit screening between DRC, Uganda, Rwanda, South Sudan, CAR and Kenya; brief national EOCs on BVD-specific clinical case definitions and rapid PCR panels that distinguish BVD from Zaire ebolavirus.

Establish emergency-use clinical-trial protocols in DRC and Uganda for investigational BVD monoclonal antibodies, remdesivir (IV and oral), and pre-clinical BVD vaccine candidates; existing Zaire-targeted countermeasures are not assumed cross-protective.

Scale isolation and ETC capacity in Bunia, Mongbwalu and Kampala; pre-position PPE and surge medevac air-ambulance contracts; brief receiving hospitals (Hamburg, London Royal Free, NIH-Bethesda, others) on BVD-specific case management and staff protections.

Communicate early and clearly: BVD spreads through direct contact with body fluids of symptomatic patients, not through airborne or casual contact. Counter stigma against travellers and Congolese diaspora; emphasize Title 42 as a screening measure, not a trade ban.
Stand up molecular epidemiology team to sequence isolates from Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Kampala and any exported cases; identify transmission chains and zoonotic reservoir(s) to guide containment.

details.First notified: 5 May 2026 (DRC MoH to WHO, unknown illness) · WHO DON 2026-DON602 published 14 May
details.Pathogen confirmed: 15 May 2026 — Bundibugyo ebolavirus on 8 samples (INRB / WHO ref lab)
details.US Title 42 order: 18 May 2026 — 30-day suspension of non-US national entry if in DRC/Uganda/South Sudan in past 21 days
details.US case #1: 18 May 2026 — Dr Peter Stafford (Bunia, since 2023); medevac to Germany with 6 high-risk-contact Americans
details.US case #2: 18 May 2026 — Independent case in Uganda confirmed by CDC
details.DRC + Uganda total (24 May): 650+ suspected · 160+ deaths (confirmed + probable) · 64 lab-confirmed · accelerating case counts
details.Index location: Mongbwalu Health Zone, Ituri Province, DRC; spread to Bunia and Rwampara health zones
details.Transmission: Direct contact with blood / body fluids of symptomatic patients; nosocomial amplification a key risk (healthcare worker deaths reported)
details.Clinical: Fever, malaise, GI symptoms → haemorrhagic phase, multi-organ failure
details.Treatment: Supportive (fluid resuscitation, oxygen); no approved BVD-specific therapeutics. Investigational mAbs and remdesivir (lab data suggest better activity against BVD than Zaire) under WHO/Africa CDC review for emergency-use trials.
details.Vaccines: None approved against BVD; rVSV-ZEBOV (Ervebo) is Zaire-specific. Several BVD vaccine candidates in pre-clinical / Phase I; emergency-use clinical-trial pathways are priority.

pathogens.name: Andes hantavirus
pathogens.scientific_name: Orthohantavirus andesense (ANDV) — MV Hondius cruise-ship cluster
pathogens.location: MV Hondius docked at Rotterdam 18 May 2026 · contacts across 19 countries
pathogens.why: The MV Hondius docked at Rotterdam on 18 May 2026. The Dutch RIVM reported no symptomatic disembarking; the remaining 25 crew and 2 medical staff entered quarantine and are undergoing clinical monitoring. Andes virus is the only hantavirus with documented human-to-human transmission, and the incubation window extends to ~6 weeks. Repatriated passengers and crew are being followed in 19 home countries. WHO still assesses global public-health risk as low, but operational burden on border health services, receiving countries' contact-tracing systems, and international clinical-alert pathways is high. No new symptomatic cases have been reported among disembarking personnel or early contacts as of 24 May.
policy_bullets: Sustain cross-border contact tracing for repatriated passengers and crew across 19 countries; incubation window extends up to ~6 weeks; median onset 14–17 days.
Support the Dutch RIVM disembarkation and disinfection protocol; provide secondary clinical-alert pathways for any contact developing fever, cough or respiratory symptoms.
Codify cruise-line protocols: rodent-exclusion, onboard isolation, cabin decontamination, passenger-screening for exposure history on embarkation.
Ensure domestic clinical-alert pathways are in place — many physicians have not seen hantavirus pulmonary syndrome; distribute clinical recognition materials to respiratory and ICU clinicians.

details.Status on disembarkation: RIVM: none of the people coming off the ship were symptomatic as of 18 May
details.Itinerary: Departed Ushuaia (Argentina) 1 April 2026; ports of call included Antarctica, South Georgia Island, Tristan da Cunha, Saint Helena, Ascension
details.Transmission: Rodent reservoir (long-tailed pygmy rice rat); rare human-to-human via close contact
details.Clinical: Fever, GI symptoms → ARDS / cardiopulmonary shock
details.Treatment: Supportive (ICU, ECMO); no licensed antiviral or vaccine
details.US risk: Extremely low — no confirmed US cases linked to the outbreak as of 24 May 2026

pathogens.name: Mpox (clade Ib)
pathogens.location: DRC, Madagascar, Uganda, Burundi, Kenya · sustained clade I transmission across ≥10 EU/EEA countries

stats.label: Clade I cases · EU/EEA · March 2026 (10 countries)
Clade I cases · EU/EEA · Jan–Mar cumulative
Unvaccinated or partially vaccinated among clade I cases

pathogens.why: ECDC's monthly mpox surveillance shows sustained clade I transmission in Europe, with 80 clade I cases reported across 10 EU/EEA countries in March 2026 (Spain leading with 23 cases), 78 in February and 89 in January — demonstrating persistent endemic circulation at moderate levels. Just 23% of reported clade I cases had completed a two-dose JYNNEOS / MVA-BN course, indicating persistent vaccination gaps despite two years of availability. Risk to MSM remains moderate; risk to general population remains low. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak and hantavirus cruise-ship cluster add operational burden on national health authorities in DRC and cross-border zones. A novel clade Ib/IIb recombinant remains flagged (WHO DON 2026-DON595) but not detected in recent surveillance.
policy_bullets: Sustain targeted JYNNEOS / MVA-BN vaccine availability for at-risk MSM groups; address coverage gap — 77% of reported clade I cases were unvaccinated or partially vaccinated.
Maintain non-stigmatizing messaging through community organizations and sexual-health clinics; avoid travel restrictions for clade Ib.
Fund continued genomic surveillance — clade I/II recombinants are emerging; ECDC's new monthly reporting will track variants in real time.
Review reimbursement codes for outpatient tecovirimat where stockpiles permit; assess clinical efficacy data from ongoing observational cohorts.

details.EU/EEA new (March 2026): 80 cases · 10 countries (Spain 23, Germany 18, Netherlands 12, Italy 11, Belgium 8, others lower)
details.Vaccine coverage among cases: 23% clade I had received 2 doses MVA-BN; 77% unvaccinated or partially vaccinated
details.Severity: Generally mild in EU/EEA — no deaths reported in clade I cases
details.Vaccines: JYNNEOS / MVA-BN (Bavarian Nordic) — limited supply in some markets; two-dose series recommended
details.Antiviral: Tecovirimat — clinical efficacy mixed in trials; outpatient access expanding
details.Recombinant flag: Clade Ib/IIb recombinant (WHO DON 2026-DON595) — genomic surveillance ongoing
